eyebrow: Azure & AWS Cloud Security Engineering · Chapter 4
titlePlain: Private Endpoints and PrivateLink: Keeping Traffic
subtitle: Lesson 15 · Network Security Across Both Clouds

code:
az network private-endpoint create \
  --name pe-storage-prod \
  --resource-group rg-prod \
  --vnet-name vnet-hub \
  --subnet subnet-pe \
  --private-connection-resource-id /subscriptions/.../storageAccounts/stprod \
  --group-id blob \
  --connection-name pe-conn-stprod
caption: A NIC with a private IP mapped to one storage account — paired with a Private DNS Zone for transparency.

code:
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0def456 \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --subnet-ids subnet-0aaa111 \
  --security-group-ids sg-0bbb222
caption: On the provider side, an NLB fronts the Endpoint Service that this ENI connects to.

steps.label: Azure Private Endpoint
steps.sub: ENI + Private DNS Zone, maps to one resource instance

steps.label: AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink)
steps.sub: ENI backed by an NLB, maps to a whole service

steps.label: AWS Gateway Endpoint (S3/DynamoDB only)
steps.sub: route table entry, no ENI, free — no Azure equivalent

eyebrow: Why this beats a firewall rule
code:
Service Endpoint (old model):
  resource keeps a public IP
  access restricted to approved VNet/subnet

Private Endpoint (this lesson):
  resource's public IP removed from the path entirely
  traffic never leaves the Microsoft backbone
caption: A firewall rule filters exposure; a Private Endpoint removes the exposure.
